rationale: THE NAMED `part of` FORM. `part of my.lib;` names a LIBRARY (declared `library my.lib;` in the owning file), not a file, and the analyzer published no row for it: the part branch only handled the URI form (`part of 'lib.dart';`). The pinned grammar parses the named form as `(part_of_directive (part_of_builtin) (dotted_identifier_list ...))` (probed) — no `string_literal`/`uri` child at all, which is why the old reader, which looked for a URI, declared the directive empty and emitted nothing. The target is the library NAME as written with inner whitespace stripped by the SAME helper the library-name reader uses, so `part of a . b;` and `library a.b;` spell one string — that string IS the module symbol's name in the store, which is what makes the row resolvable (strategy 2, unique name). The direction is the directive's own direction: this file is the PART, so partRole is "part". `isNamedLibrary` records the spelling form so a consumer can tell it from the URI form without re-reading the source.

expectRelationships.note: THE NEW ROW — the whole point of this fixture. Before the fix the directive produced NOTHING: there is no string_literal/uri child to unquote, and the branch only pushed a row when the URI was non-empty.
the fixture's ordinary content must still publish its reads — a fix that returned early at the directive must not swallow the rest of the file.

forbidRelationships.note: THE NAMED PART-OF DIRECTIVE IS NOT AN IMPORT — it is a part/library coupling, the canonical `part_of` label.
the retired specifier shape: a named library is a name, never a `name:*` URI stand-in.

WHITESPACE STRIPPED — the target must be the same spelling `library a.b;` publishes (`my.lib`), or the store cannot bind the two sides of one library name. The grammar accepts `part of my . lib;` and this fixture's source writes it tight; the pin makes the normalisation visible.
